title: Monotonicity of symmetric adjacency
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$ and two vertices $u, v \in \mathrm{Fin}\,n$, and let $e_1$ and $e_2$ be lists of weighted edges on $n$ vertices such that every edge of $e_1$ also occurs in $e_2$. If $u$ and $v$ are symmetrically adjacent in $e_1$ — that is, some edge of $e_1$ has endpoints $\{u,v\}$ in either order — then $u$ and $v$ are symmetrically adjacent in $e_2$.
hypotheses_covered: u and v are symmetrically adjacent in the edge list e1
every edge of e1 also belongs to e2
replaced:
If $\mathtt{SymAdj}\,e_1\,u\,v$ and every edge of $e_1$ also belongs to $e_2$, then
$\mathtt{SymAdj}\,e_2\,u\,v$.
